prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. PRODUCTION DIFFUSE TEXTURE ATLAS, not a concept sheet and not 3D product mockups. Make an opaque 1536x1024 landscape image divided into EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 2 equal rows, no gaps, no border lines, eight rectangular label panels. Reference image is our existing DarkWinter provision label atlas; match its coarse hand-painted paper, muted ink and clear old grocery illustrations, but make these eight original product labels. Canadian/Alaskan remote grocery supplies in the 1990s, a few days after a disaster: mostly intact, faint handling scuffs, no rot, no snow. Matte cream or kraft paper, desaturated navy/olive/brick/ochre inks. Each tile is a front packaging label in orthographic flat view, art filling the rectangle with full-bleed simple paper and generous margins. Short text perfectly readable, facing viewer, no perspective, no bottles, no actual boxes, no metal, no background scene, no shadows outside panels. One centered uppercase product heading near upper third, an original large simple painted ingredient illustration beneath. No brand logos or additional slogans, no barcodes required. Label order from left to right, top row then bottom row: 1. CORN: yellow corn cob, olive and ochre; 2. PEAS: green peas in an open pod, muted green; 3. TOMATOES: two red tomatoes, brick red; 4. PEACHES: peach halves, faded orange; 5. MUSHROOM SOUP: mushrooms and bowl, dark brown; 6. CHICKEN SOUP: chicken and noodles in bowl, ochre/navy; 7. PEANUT BUTTER: peanuts, tan/brown; 8. BERRY JAM: raspberry and dark red berries, burgundy. Tile dimensions must be exactly equal and aligned. Do not repeat illustrations from the reference. Do not add numbering. Avoid glossy modern graphics, photorealism, vanilla Minecraft pixel icons and generic random procedural noise.
